Ensampble of the two models' (LDA and GLMM) candidate ranks

Library
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)
library(pROC)
library(lme4)
```

Data
```{r}
# --- MASTER DATA PREPARATION ---
data_full <- read.csv("./data/sp_level_data.csv") %>% 
  # Ensure random effects are factors
  mutate(Family = as.factor(Family))

# A. Filter & Prep
data_m1 <- data_full %>%
  filter(group %in% c("Natives - Red Sea", "Lessepsians - Red Sea")) %>%
  mutate(
    # Create Binary Response: Natives=0, NIS=1
    response = ifelse(group == "Lessepsians - Red Sea", 1, 0),
    group_label = droplevels(factor(group)),
    Family = droplevels(Family)
  )
```

#1. Training data & model Evaluation
##1.1) Calculate AUC & weights
```{r}
# Extract training probabilities
# 1. Load the, Out-of-Sample Probabilities for the LDA
lda_cv_data <- read.csv("./models/A)_Native_range_comparison_cv_probs.csv")

# 2. Get Out-of-Sample Probabilities for the GLMM (LOOCV Loop)
# STEP A: Create an empty container (a blank list of numbers) to hold our predictions.
# We make it exactly as long as our dataset (e.g., 126 blank spaces).
glmm_cv_probs <- numeric(nrow(data_m1))
# STEP B: Load the original model. 
# We just need its structure (the formula, random effects, etc.)
final_glmm <- read_rds("./models/native_r_comp_glmm.rds")

# STEP C: Start the "Hide and Seek" Loop.
# "for(i in 1:nrow(data_m1))" means: "Run the code inside these brackets 126 times. 
# The first time, i=1. The second time, i=2... all the way to the end."
for(i in 1:nrow(data_m1)) {
  # 1. CREATE THE TRAINING DATA (The 125 fish the model is allowed to see)
  # The minus sign [-i, ] means "Give me all rows EXCEPT row number i"
  train_data <- data_m1[-i, ]
  # 2. CREATE THE TEST DATA (The 1 hidden fish)
  # [i, ] means "Give me exactly row number i". 
  # 'drop = FALSE' just forces R to keep it as a dataframe format instead of turning it into a raw vector.
  test_data  <- data_m1[i, , drop = FALSE]
  # 3. TRAIN THE TEMPORARY MODEL
  # 'update()' takes our original model  and refits it using ONLY our 125 train_data fish.
  cv_model <- suppressWarnings(update(final_glmm, data = train_data))
  # 4. PREDICT THE HIDDEN FISH
  # We ask the newly trained 'cv_model' to predict the risk for our 1 hidden 'test_data' fish.
  # 'type = "response"' ensures it outputs a probability (0 to 1).
  # 're.form = NA' tells the model to ignore random effects (like 'Family') when making this prediction, 
  # focusing only on the main fixed effects (the traits).
  # Finally, we save that single number into slot 'i' of our empty container from Step A.
  glmm_cv_probs[i] <- predict(cv_model, newdata = test_data, type = "response", re.form = NA)
}
# The loop finishes, and 'glmm_cv_probs' is now a full list of 126, out-of-sample predictions

# 3. Create a unified dataframe for the training calculations
train_cv_data <- data_m1 %>%
  select(species, response) %>%
  mutate(glmm_cv_prob = glmm_cv_probs) %>%
  left_join(lda_cv_data, by = "species") %>%
  na.omit() # Ensures we only calculate on species present in both models

# 4. Calculate the, Cross-Validated ROC and AUC for both models
roc_glmm_cv <- roc(train_cv_data$response, train_cv_data$glmm_cv_prob, quiet = TRUE)
roc_lda_cv  <- roc(train_cv_data$response, train_cv_data$lda_cv_prob, quiet = TRUE)

auc_glmm_cv <- as.numeric(auc(roc_glmm_cv))
auc_glmm_cv
auc_lda_cv  <- as.numeric(auc(roc_lda_cv))
auc_lda_cv

# 5. Calculate True Performance Weights based on the CV-AUC
total_cv_auc <- auc_glmm_cv + auc_lda_cv
w_glmm <- auc_glmm_cv / total_cv_auc
w_lda  <- auc_lda_cv / total_cv_auc

print(paste("GLMM LOOCV AUC:", round(auc_glmm_cv, 3), "| Weight:", round(w_glmm, 3)))
print(paste("LDA LOOCV AUC:", round(auc_lda_cv, 3), "| Weight:", round(w_lda, 3)))

# 6. Find the  Optimal Threshold using the Cross-Validated Ensemble
cv_ensemble_index <- (train_cv_data$glmm_cv_prob * w_glmm) + (train_cv_data$lda_cv_prob * w_lda)
roc_cv_ensemble <- roc(train_cv_data$response, cv_ensemble_index, quiet = TRUE)

opt_coords <- coords(roc_cv_ensemble, "best", ret = c("threshold", "specificity", "sensitivity"), best.method="youden")
optimal_thresh <- opt_coords$threshold[1]
```

Plot ROC
```{r}
# Create a tiny dataframe 
optimal_point_df <- data.frame(
  specificity = opt_coords$specificity[1],
  sensitivity = opt_coords$sensitivity[1]
)

p_roc <- ggroc(roc_cv_ensemble, colour = "darkblue", linewidth = 1) +
  
  theme_classic() +
  
  # Add the diagonal "random chance" reference line
  geom_abline(intercept = 1, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  
  # FIX: Correctly map the X and Y coordinates for the red dot
  geom_point(data = optimal_point_df, 
             aes(x = specificity, y = sensitivity), 
             color = "red", size = 4) +
  
  # Add a text label next to the dot
  annotate("text", 
           x = opt_coords$specificity[1] + 0.15, 
           y = opt_coords$sensitivity[1] - 0.05, 
           label = paste0("Optimal cutoff:\n", round(optimal_thresh, 3)),
           color = "red", fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
           
  labs(
    x = "Specificity (True negative rate)",
    y = "Sensitivity (True positive rate)",
    caption = paste0("LOOCV Area Under the Curve (AUC): ", round(auc(roc_cv_ensemble), 3))
  ) +
  
  theme(
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 10, face = "italic")
  )

p_roc
ggsave("./plots/Figure_ROC_Curve.png", p_roc, width = 15, height = 12, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
```

#2. Build the Performance-Weighted Ensemble for Future Candidates
Now we apply the weights and threshold  derived above to the native species pool to predict future invaders.
```{r}
# Load predictions for the candidate pool
pred_lda  <- read.csv("./models/lda_1_posterior_output_df.csv")
pred_glmm <- read.csv("./models/watchlist_glmm_best_model.csv")

# Merge, weight, and rank
ensemble_data <- pred_glmm %>%
  select(species, Family, glmm_probs = Probability) %>%
  left_join(pred_lda %>% select(species, lda_probs = probs), by = "species") %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  mutate(
    ensemble_index = (glmm_probs * w_glmm) + (lda_probs * w_lda),
    
    # CALCULATE RANKS
    rank_glmm = dense_rank(desc(glmm_probs)),
    rank_lda  = dense_rank(desc(lda_probs)),
    rank_ensemble = dense_rank(desc(ensemble_index)),
    
    # Consensus Group based on Empirically Derived Threshold
    consensus_group = case_when(
      glmm_probs > optimal_thresh & lda_probs > optimal_thresh ~ "High consensus",
      glmm_probs > optimal_thresh ~ "GLMM only",
      lda_probs > optimal_thresh ~ "LDA only",
      TRUE ~ "Low consensus"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(ensemble_index))

# Lock in factor levels for plotting colors later
ensemble_data$consensus_group <- factor(
  ensemble_data$consensus_group,
  levels = c("High consensus", "GLMM only", "LDA only", "Low consensus")
)

# Display and Save
head(ensemble_data)
write.csv(ensemble_data, "./models/watchlist_ensemble.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

#3. Assess Model Similarity & Plot (Figure 5)
```{r}
# A. Statistical Correlation (Spearman Rank Correlation)
cor_test <- cor.test(ensemble_data$rank_glmm, ensemble_data$rank_lda, method = "spearman")

print(paste0("Spearman Correlation between LDA and GLMM Ranks: rho = ", 
             round(cor_test$estimate, 2), 
             " (p-value: ", signif(cor_test$p.value, 3), ")"))

# B. Top 20 Overlap Calculation
top_20_glmm <- ensemble_data %>% filter(rank_glmm <= 20) %>% pull(species)
top_20_lda  <- ensemble_data %>% filter(rank_lda <= 20)  %>% pull(species)
shared_spp  <- intersect(top_20_glmm, top_20_lda)

print(paste0("Number of species shared in the Top 20 of both models: ", length(shared_spp)))
print(paste("Shared species:", paste(shared_spp, collapse = ", ")))

# C. Visual Comparison (Scatter Plot)

# DYNAMICALLY EXTRACT TOP 10 LABELS:
# Sort the dataframe by  final ensemble rank and pull the top 10 species names.
top_10_labels <- ensemble_data %>%
  arrange(desc(ensemble_index)) %>% # Change 'ensemble_rank' if  column name is different
  slice(1:10) %>%
  pull(species)

custom_breaks <- c(1, seq(20, 140, by = 20))

p_agreement <- ggplot(ensemble_data, aes(x = rank_lda, y = rank_glmm)) +
  
  geom_point(aes(color = consensus_group, label=species), alpha = 0.85, size = 2) +
  
  # Apply the dynamic top 10 labels here
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
    data = subset(ensemble_data, species %in% top_10_labels),
    aes(label = species),
    size = 3.25,
    fontface = "italic",
    box.padding = 0.6,
    max.overlaps = Inf,
    segment.alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  
  scale_color_manual(values = c("High consensus" = "red", 
                                "GLMM only" = "purple", 
                                "LDA only" = "brown", 
                                "Low consensus" = "grey80")) +
  
  scale_x_reverse(name = "LDA rank",
                  breaks = custom_breaks,       
                  limits = c(145, 1),            
                  expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0))) + 
  
  scale_y_reverse(name = "GLMM rank",
                  breaks = custom_breaks,       
                  limits = c(145, 1),          
                  expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0))) +
  
  theme_classic() +
  
  theme(
    legend.position = c(0.76, 0.35), 
    legend.justification = c("left", "top"),
    legend.direction = "vertical",
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    legend.box.background = element_blank(),
    legend.key = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size=10),
    plot.caption = element_text(size=10)
  ) +
  
  labs(caption = paste0("Spearman ρ: ", round(cor_test$estimate, 2)),
       color = "Consensus group") + 
  
  coord_cartesian(xlim=c(110,-5), ylim=c(70,-5))

p_agreement

# Save Outputs
ggsave("./plots/Figure_5.png", p_agreement, width = 18, height = 12, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
ggsave("./plots/Figure_5.pdf", p_agreement, width = 18, height = 12, units = "cm", dpi = 300,device = "pdf")
```
